osaka_menya_75hz_kuromon.hours_raw: Open 24 hours; closed Thursday and the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of each month (Tabelog). One staff member on at a time (October 2026). A service charge may be added (Tabelog). No reservations. Cards, e-money and QR accepted.
osaka_menya_75hz_kuromon.notes: [Ramen · 24-hour Takaida-style shoyu ramen by Kuromon] A cramped ten-seat counter by Kuromon Market serving Takaida-style ramen around the clock; it's closed only Thursdays and the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays. Reviewers call the brand "7.5Hz" or "Nanahan". The bowl is a rich, sharp soy broth with more acidity than one visitor expected, thick straight noodles with low moisture, and chashu, best with an extra heap of chopped green onion. One reviewer who knows the original Takaida shop found the same chashu and noodles here, with a slightly milder broth. Chuka soba is ¥800 and a large chashu ramen ¥1,100 (September–October 2026). There's a garlic spice on the counter. People drop in after a night out, or for a morning bowl at 8 am. One person works the shop at a time, and a service charge may be added.

chef_bio.background: A Kuromon branch of the Takaida-style ramen shop Menya 7.5Hz (September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "While the service differs from the Takai-da branch, the basic concept remains the same. The flavor of the chashu is identical, and the noodles taste the same as well. However, the broth seems slightly milder here." — September 2026.
"The broth, which had a stronger acidity than I expected. The noodles were straight and had a low moisture content." — October 2026, late night, chuka soba with green onions.

Touch-panel ticket machine at the entrance; noodle firmness asked when you hand over the ticket (September 2026). No reservations. Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_tenchijin_ramen_2gouten.notes: [Ramen · light tonkotsu shoyu beside Nankai Namba] A 16-seat counter right beside Nankai Namba Station, open since 2019 and good value. Every ramen here is pork-bone based, and though it looks rich and fatty it eats surprisingly light, with a depth of dashi and medium-thick noodles that soak it up. Generous crunchy green onions add to that. Say how firm you want the noodles when you hand over your ticket. Pickled ginger from the counter works well with the tonkotsu. The ramen-and-pork-bowl set is ¥1,280 (September 2026), and the pork is stir-fried after you order. There's also abura soba (¥1,000) with three slices of chashu, spicy meat mazesoba that can sell out, and tsukemen with a free large size. One diner found it a bit salty. Tabelog only says it opens at 11:00, so check closing times.

"The broth was a bit lighter, but it had a rich tonkotsu flavor with a nice depth from the dashi… the combination of tonkotsu and ginger was fantastic." — September 2026, original-flavor ramen and pork-bowl set ¥1,280.

osaka_hard_romanticker_namba.notes: [Standing bar · a Tabelog 100 tachinomi with no sign, behind Namba] A small standing bar just off Midosuji near Namba Hips, named to Tabelog's 2025 standing-bar 100 and a sister of Oishi Stand. There's no sign, so it's easy to walk past; the shop's Instagram says to look for it. It gets packed; one evening a regular shuffled over to make room. Reviewers note many women among the crowd, unusual for a tachinomi. Small plates make it easy to try a lot. The cream cheese with crackers, slightly sweet, won over one reviewer who doesn't usually like cream cheese, and the blue cheese has fans too. There's Shine Muscat with prosciutto as shira-ae, an Ezo venison steak served rare, and house satsuma-age with cheese, corn and edamame, fried after you order. A hamburger is limited to three servings. Expect ¥2,000–4,000. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_kokopelli_namba.notes: [Burgers · American burgers and world beer by Hozenji] A stylish American-style burger bar a few steps from the Hozenji entrance, open since 2011 and drawing overseas guests too. The toasted buns get singled out; one burger hunter ranked it in a personal top three, buns especially. The cheeseburger is ¥1,480, plus ¥350 for a drink (July 2026). The bacon cheeseburger layers thick bacon over a juicy patty, and the avocado burger is creamy and rich. The tender pulled pork with an addictive barbecue sauce looks as good as it does on Instagram. A macaroni-topped burger has been on TV. The grilled-cheese sandwich comes on toasted whole-wheat bread with thick bacon and avocado, and the chef adjusted the cheese on request. The fries are crisp without being greasy. There's a long list of bottled beers from around the world. Lunch is burgers only. Closed Mondays.

osaka_gendai_kappou_hozenji_momo.notes: [Japanese · a hidden creative kappo by Hozenji Yokocho] A creative kappo counter with private rooms, tucked deep inside a nondescript building by Hozenji Yokocho, open since 2021. Finding the door takes some effort. The kitchen builds colorful courses on Japanese seasonal tradition. Lunch is the easy way in: a weekday mini course with seasonal clay-pot rice for ¥3,000, or ¥5,000 for more. Recent courses ran from a lotus-root dumpling in vivid broccoli sauce to fried sanma served as a salad, with crispy okra among the starters. The clay-pot rice, chestnut in autumn or corn, scallop and shiso in summer, leaves enough for seconds, and what's left is made into rice balls to take home. Several diners praise the tableware and care. One critic found the dishes pre-plated and the egg rice hard and clumped. Dinner runs about ¥8,000–15,000. Closed most Tuesdays.

Reservations accepted; at dinner, groups with children are seated in a private room. A 5% year-end fee applies 15 December–4 January (Tabelog). Cards, QUICPay, PayPay and Alipay accepted.
osaka_teppanyaki_zin_namba.notes: [Teppanyaki · Kobe-beef teppanyaki with a Dotonbori night view] A 14-seat teppanyaki counter on the eighth floor above Yoshinoya, looking out over the lights of Dotonbori. The head chef came up through luxury hotels (reviewers name the St. Regis Osaka and the Ritz), and the cooking shows it. You choose black wagyu, Matsusaka or Kobe beef for the omakase. A 14-course black-wagyu strip loin course was ¥12,000 (April 2026), and an anniversary course with tenderloin ¥16,000. Beyond the steak, diners rave about the seafood: crisp-skinned sea bass with shiso genovese, and teppan-fried Nagasaki horse mackerel with a pickle tartar, one diner's best ever. Wagyu dumplings in consommé and seared wagyu sushi round it out, and rice cooked in a kamado from Kyoto's Gihei closes the meal. One diner found the seasoning a little salty. Many guests are from abroad; the menu is in English and staff speak English.

chef_bio.background: Head chef trained in hotel kitchens, previously at the St. Regis Osaka and the Ritz (July 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Some dishes run a food-cost ratio above 40% (July 2026 review).

osaka_nipponbashi_sakaichi.notes: [Ramen · a six-seat morning-ramen counter in Shimanouchi] A six-seat counter in Shimanouchi, rated 3.64 on Tabelog, open since 2022 and run by the owner with one helper. It opens at 7 am on weekends, and lines can form outside by 8. The regular menu is shoyu: a chicken and seafood broth that's easy to drink to the last drop, chewy flat whole-wheat noodles from Menya Teikaku, and in the Shoyu Special (¥1,600) four kinds of chashu, from low-temperature chicken breast to hanging-roasted pork belly. The fun is the rotating bowls announced on social media. Recent ones included a cement-gray niboshi soba from Himi sardines that is clean, with no bitterness, a clear niboshi-and-scallop shio, a thick crab-and-scallop shio, and a tachiuo tsukemen with a raw-egg kamatama dip. Finish with a ¥100 bowl of rice in the leftover soup. There are no table condiments. Cash only, and bring small notes for the machine. One first-timer singled out the owner's service. Check X or Instagram for closures.

It's light, with the pork's richness coming through without the heaviness, and plenty of thinly sliced chashu over smooth thin noodles. One diner found it strongly salty, another wanted more punch. A menu revamp on 17 September 2026 added a back-fat chuka soba with rice for ¥880, and there's a spicy umami soba (¥1,000) with optional extra heat. Bottled beer and a ¥500 snack plate of toppings make it a quick drinking stop.

The draw is hong shao beef noodles, rich and aromatic with real Sichuan-pepper numbing. There are also premium beef noodles, a spicy beef noodle soup with tender marinated beef and chewy noodles, and a fat-intestine version. Add honeycomb tripe. You pick the numbing and the heat, and even "mild" makes people sweat. One diner found medium numbing and medium spice perfectly balanced. There's no rice to finish. Closed Sundays. Cash only.

Check sake prices, which add up fast. One September diner found the meat tough and the hygiene off-putting. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

The signature (¥820, September 2026) arrives as one serving split into two small bowls, a nod to a married couple, and ordering it as a couple is said to bring luck. Don't share: it's one order per guest. The zenzai is made with Tanba Dainagon azuki, gently sweet and a little thick, with a few whole beans and a soft rice-cake dumpling. Salt kombu and green tea cut the sweetness, and staff refill the tea. In summer there's a chilled zenzai, plus matcha-azuki kakigori. Today it's run by the Wasyoku Sato group and open 10 am to 10 pm, handy for dessert after takoyaki. There's a shelf of Meoto Zenzai souvenirs.

osaka_menya_joroku_namba.notes: [Ramen · Takaida-style black chuka soba, a Tabelog 100 regular] A seven-seat counter down a narrow alley near NGK, named to Tabelog's ramen 100 every year from 2017 to 2025, with lines and a waiting area at lunch. It opened in 2008 at Tempozan Marketplace and moved to Namba in 2010. The chuka soba is Takaida-style: a broth that looks nearly black and smells strongly of soy, yet drinks lighter and less salty than you'd expect, with black pepper on top. Medium-thick straight noodles soak it up, with thin chashu, menma and green onion. A small is ¥900 and a regular ¥1,000 (October 2026). Add the ¥200 hayazushi, vinegared rice wrapped in leaves from Wakayama. There's also a shrimp shio with sakura shrimp and niboshi, limited bowls such as a garlic ramen on special days, and on the first Sunday of the month it opens at 7 am for morning ramen. A Hokkaido visitor found the soy too assertive. Cash only; closed Wednesdays.

osaka_tonsha_malatang_nagahoribashi.notes: [Chinese · build-your-own malatang by Nagahoribashi] A two-floor malatang and hot-pot shop two minutes from Nagahoribashi, part of the Tonsha group, with a calm counter downstairs and private rooms upstairs. The broth leans more numbing than hot, with real umami, and level 1 already has a kick. Fans recommend winter melon, white fungus, shrimp balls and knife-cut or sweet-potato noodles (two noodle types at most), with the sesame sauce and free green onion, coriander and garlic piled on. There's also a tomato mala soup with sweetness and acidity. Hot-pot courses run in the evening.

The draw is the negiyaki "Fujiyama", heaped with green onion over tender beef tendon; one visitor came back a year later just for it. The batter is made with soy milk and nagaimo for a smooth texture, and the sauce is a house blend of Osaka sauces. There's also a seafood negiyaki packed with shrimp and octopus, a well-balanced mixed okonomiyaki, a modan-yaki with chewy noodles and the popular tonpeiyaki, with around 30 shochu to drink. Sets for two let you try a mini negiyaki and two okonomiyaki. Prices are low for the area, and there's an English menu. No reservations; closed Mondays.

À la carte there's meaty crab, big shrimp-and-chive dumplings and a shochu highball made with a whole lemon. Shared dishes come portioned for two, and there's a good wine list with pairings. Lunch is a chef's select course for one group a day, booked three days ahead. The master seems gruff at first but warms up. Note the tipping system and one-drink policy, and leave big luggage in a locker. Closed irregularly.

Cuts run about ¥1,500–2,000 each (January 2026): thick salted tongue to finish with lemon, kuri, hanging tender, nakaochi, thin top blade and tripe. It fills up on Fridays, but same-day online booking sometimes works. There's a ¥500 cover charge. Closed Sundays.

osaka_shiru_hisa_hozenji.notes: [Kushikatsu · creative kushikatsu beside Hozenji since 1946] A calm, jazz-playing kushikatsu counter right next to Mizukake Fudo in Hozenji Yokocho, from a kushikatsu house founded in 1946, with sister branches elsewhere. Thirty to forty creative skewers use seasonal ingredients in a light, crisp batter, each with its own sauce. The fun is the omakase: skewers keep coming one by one until you say stop. There are set courses too, such as a ¥5,720 seasonal course of ten skewers with fresh vegetables, a drink and ochazuke or rice with red miso soup (January 2025). Favorites include beef tenderloin, shrimp, pork, clams and whiting, and dessert might be a fig, with jasmine tea to close. One diner who has been coming for more than 50 years says it never sits heavy. Expect ¥8,000–15,000. Closed Thursdays.

Unlike the thick shrimp-miso style, the ebi shio here is light and gentle: a clear chicken-bone broth with a sauce from sweet shrimp, and the shrimp flavor hits from the first sip. It's ¥950, or ¥1,350 as the special (May and October 2026) with two wontons, bean sprouts and a hint of yuzu. You pick your chashu from thick pork belly, pork shoulder or fatty beef. The Kiwami Kuromon shoyu layers several soy sauces over chicken, pork, shrimp and scallop, with medium-thin noodles from Mie's Ayahikari flour; one diner found the soy drowned the shrimp. Most customers are visitors, and there's a short line at weekend lunch. Pay after eating, in cash.

Downstairs you stand around the kitchen; upstairs is seated (¥330) with mobile ordering and its own menu. Big platters of daily obanzai line the counter. Bigger dishes include crab-miso cream croquettes, sanma confit with eggplant purée and rare wild boar with red wine sauce. Drinks run to mega highballs, fruit sours and a grated-peach bellini, and you can grab bottled beer from the self-service fridge.

A newer herbal hot-pot course piles leafy greens into a gentle Chinese-style broth, then chicken, pork and beef with an egg dip, and udon to finish. There are kara-age and drinking snacks, free karaoke and TV for sports. Smoking is allowed throughout. ¥300 charge; cash only; closed Mondays.

The Gyoton!! balances seafood umami with pork sweetness. Rice is ¥100 with free refills, so pour broth over it and add the table's doubanjiang and garlic. Reviewers call it a solid, classic bowl rather than a standout, and one found it a bit salty. Office workers line up at lunch. Cash only.

osaka_ramen_kurumu_kitahorie.notes: [Ramen · morning wonton noodles in Kitahorie] An 11-seat counter in Kitahorie, three minutes from Yotsubashi, open since October 2023 from 8 am until the soup runs out, so noon visitors sometimes find it closed. The draw is the wontons: springy shrimp ones and juicy pork ones in big, slippery wrappers; the pork and shrimp wonton noodles are ¥1,200 (September–October 2026). Medium-thin noodles and thin, wide chashu complete it. One reviewer found the table pepper unnecessary. Expect a short line most mornings. Cash only.

osaka_menya_teru_nagahoribashi.notes: [Tsukemen · seafood-tonkotsu tsukemen by Nagahoribashi] A 12-seat counter two minutes from Nagahoribashi, a branch (since 2011) of a group known for seafood tonkotsu, with its head office in Higashiyodogawa. The broth simmers pork bones and vegetables until they dissolve, then adds seafood and kombu, for a dark, thick, additive-free dip with a gentle flavor. Tsukemen is ¥1,050, or ¥1,150 with a seasoned egg (June 2026), and one repeat visitor loves the chashu and noodles in the large chashu tsukemen. The onsen-tamago special ramen has a niboshi-forward fish tonkotsu, easy to drink, on medium-thin firm noodles. Limited bowls rotate: rich niboshi or spicy tsukemen, a standout chilled curry ramen, a mackerel ramen. One diner wanted the dip hotter and the noodles chewier. The listed hours aren't always kept, so check first. Cash only.

osaka_egokoro_champon_nambanaka.notes: [Champon · white and red champon near Namba Parks] A classic neighborhood Chinese shop near Namba Parks, three minutes from Nankai Namba, serving champon since 2008, with regulars who have come for years. The white champon is a rich yet smooth pork-bone broth with finely chopped toppings; the red is a chicken-bone broth with Sichuan doubanjiang, mildly spicy. Both use chewy medium-thick champon noodles. For ¥50 more it becomes a set with rice, which you can drop into the leftover soup like porridge; a set with fried rice is ¥1,200. Follow the table guide and add vinegar and chili oil partway. There's sara udon too. Cash only; smoking allowed. Closed Saturdays and holidays.

The chicken-and-pork version adds seared meat, and spicy limited bowls run from "Shakunetsu no Rei" to the hotter "Yogan" cold tantan with diced meat, which left one diner's mouth sore. A small ginger soup comes first, and weekday lunch adds rice or ice cream. Cash only.

osaka_mita_seimenjo_namba_city.notes: [Tsukemen · Mita Seimenjo inside Namba CITY] A 44-seat branch of the Mita Seimenjo tsukemen chain on the first floor of Namba CITY's South Building, a separate shop from the chain's Sennichimae branch. It's rarely crowded. Order by QR code; noodles are boiled fresh, so allow 10 minutes or more. The big perk: anything from 200 g to 500 g of noodles costs the same. Wheaty, medium-thick noodles go with a reliable rich tsukemen, a spicy version, or a light chilled sea-bream shio tsukemen with yuzu peel; you can choose hot or cold noodles. On the 3rd of each month a coupon makes all toppings free. The kara-age is better than you'd expect. One diner found the toppings ice-cold with cold noodles, and another the chashu a little tough.

anecdotes.text: "You can choose between 200g to 500g of noodles for the same price!… The sea bream broth is perfect for those who prefer a lighter taste! The yuzu peel and seaweed added a nice touch." — August 2026, chilled sea-bream shio tsukemen with all toppings.

"I chose the rich tsukemen and was amazed that I could even select the temperature of the noodles… The taste was reliably good, though I was disappointed that the chashu was a bit tough." — September 2026.

osaka_kinmugi_namba.notes: [Ramen · Kinmugi's chicken paitan by Nankai Namba] The second shop of Kinmugi, after the Amerikamura original, opened in September 2025 on a back street two minutes from Nankai Namba's west exit, with a clean, elegant interior and good service. The chicken paitan ramen (¥1,000, August–October 2026) is creamy and frothy, sweet and gentle rather than heavy, with chicken and pork chashu and a well-cooked soft-boiled egg. The tsukemen (¥1,100, large +¥150) pairs a light, foamy paitan dip with chilled thick curly noodles. Add a ¥300 yodare-chicken rice bowl. Summer brought a chilled corn-potage noodle with sweet potato, broccoli and chicken. There's sometimes a short line. Buy at the touch-panel machine; cards and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Second Kinmugi shop after the Amerikamura branch, run by Mugikyu Co., Ltd. (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The chicken paitan ramen arrived, looking rich and creamy, reminiscent of a stew, with a beautifully cooked soft-boiled egg… both chicken and pork chashu." — August 2026, ramen ¥1,000 and yodare-chicken rice bowl ¥300.
"The dipping sauce was a light and frothy chicken paitan, paired with thick noodles that had a nice bite after being chilled in cold water." — September 2026, tsukemen ¥1,100.
